# This is a RE-CHECK of a revised two-paragraph scientific summary of PRIMARY (aut

**Question:** This is a RE-CHECK of a revised two-paragraph scientific summary of PRIMARY (autoantibody-associated) MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY. An earlier version was reviewed and returned needs_revision for four reasons: (a) it claimed the antigens form "one shared antigen-autoantibody mechanism rather than separate diseases per antigen", judged too strong against antigen-based classification; (b) it omitted NELL1 and its "under 1-4.9%" frequency figure was wrong if read as covering the whole non-PLA2R/THSD7A remainder; (c) it omitted anti-PLA2R titre as an activity correlate, epitope spreading, and non-IgG4 subclasses; (d) its primary-versus-secondary framing was dated. Do your own independent literature search; do not agree from memory. Evidence cutoff 2026-10-13. Secondary membranous nephropathy and therapy efficacy are deliberately OUT OF SCOPE.

REVISED SUMMARY — Paragraph 1: "Primary membranous nephropathy shares an antigen-specific podocyte autoantibody principle, but antigen-defined subtypes differ in frequency, serology and clinical associations and are increasingly treated as partly distinct entities. Autoantibodies, IgG4-predominant though not IgG4-exclusive, bind a podocyte surface antigen: PLA2R in most inspected adult cases, THSD7A in a smaller PLA2R-negative subgroup, NELL-1 in a substantial further share of PLA2R-negative cases with primary-disease features, and semaphorin 3B, HTRA1 or rarer putative targets beyond those. In each case the antigen localized to podocytes or to the subepithelial deposits, and deposit-eluted or patient serum IgG recognized it. Anti-PLA2R levels tracked clinical status and proteinuria, and epitope spreading beyond the cysteine-rich domain was an independent risk factor for poor renal outcome. HLA-DQA1 and PLA2R1 risk loci were associated with biopsy-proven disease in white-ancestry cohorts."

Paragraph 2: "Antigen-specific rodent models supply the directional evidence: podocyte expression of human PLA2R1 produced antibodies, subepithelial deposits and nephrotic syndrome, lymphocyte-deficient animals developed neither, and Thsd7a-knockout mice were protected from antibody transfer. These do not show that every human subtype shares one effector route. Complement is consistently involved but heterogeneously so. All three initiation pathways were present in patient biopsies with proximity assays favouring the classical pathway, yet factor-B-null mice were protected and lectin-pathway blockade preserved synaptopodin and NEPH1 in podocyte culture; no initiating route is established as universal in humans. Effector evidence conflicts directly: C5b-9 assembly was required for slit-protein proteolysis in culture and C5 deficiency partly reduced albuminuria, while membrane-attack-complex inhibition left albumin permselectivity unchanged on a glomerulus-on-a-chip and anti-THSD7A antibodies injured podocytes in C3-deficient mice. The under-1-to-4.9% frequencies apply only to the seven putative mass-spectrometry targets, not to NELL-1. Scope is restricted to primary disease by curation choice, not because the primary-secondary split is current practice; claims rest on agent-inspected abstracts, no therapy is curated, and appraisals are uncalibrated."

TASKS, answered explicitly and in order:
1. For each of the four prior issues (a)-(d), state RESOLVED / PARTIALLY RESOLVED / NOT RESOLVED, with reasoning and citations.
2. NEW OVERALL VERDICT: exactly one of consistent_with_caveats / needs_revision / insufficient_evidence.
3. Any REMAINING major errors, unsupported statements or causal overstatement in the revised text.
4. Any remaining material omissions that a bounded summary of this declared scope should not omit.
5. Is the characterisation of the complement debate (no universal initiating route; C5b-9 not settled as principal effector) accurate as of 2026?
6. Is "NELL-1 in a substantial further share of PLA2R-negative cases with primary-disease features" an accurate characterisation, or does it over- or under-state NELL-1's role and its association with malignancy?
Report your actual search coverage and date range. If you cannot retrieve current literature for any part, say so explicitly rather than agreeing from memory.

# **Re-Check** of Revised **Primary MN** Summary

Search coverage spanned four targeted queries on antigen-based classification, NELL1 frequency/malignancy, anti-PLA2R titre/epitope spreading/subclasses, and complement mechanisms; the retrieved set was then deduplicated and ranked, and this assessment uses the 20 supplied papers with publication dates from **2018-06-22 to 2026-09-08**. No outside papers beyond the supplied set were retrievable here, so points below are limited to what these indexed papers support directly.

## Primary Membranous Nephropathy

| Evidence Strength | Claim |
|---|---|
| Evidence strength: Strong (9/10) | **Antigen-based classification** is well supported, and several reviews explicitly treat PLA2R-, THSD7A-, NELL1-, SEMA3B-, and other antigen-associated forms as **distinct entities** with differing clinicopathologic associations [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenic-spectrum-in-membranous-nephropathy-a-jain-tiwari/0f14bc45db215165b39c77afd0ad9815/) |
| Evidence strength: Strong (8/10) | **NELL1 should not be lumped** into a generic “under 1–4.9%” remainder: its reported frequency varies by denominator and cohort, from about **1.5–2% of whole primary MN cohorts** to **3.8–35% of PLA2R/THSD7A-negative groups** [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/prevalence-of-neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-and-iwakura-ema/366a2a3e31465da3ad412bfb43fc911c/) [[4.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factor–like-1-protein–positive-wang-sun/f6e85d3069095577b934153447ca82ad/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) |
| Evidence strength: Strong (8/10) | **Anti-PLA2R biology is not IgG4-exclusive**: other subclasses are common, anti-PLA2R levels track disease activity, and epitope spreading beyond **CysR** is linked to worse outcomes, though some prognostic incremental value remains debated [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[9.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[10.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/) [[10.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/) |

**Figure 1:** Strength of evidence for the four revision issues

## Issue-by-Issue Disposition

1. **(a) Shared mechanism vs distinct antigen-defined diseases: RESOLVED.**  
The revision no longer claims one undifferentiated shared mechanism; it now says subtypes are “partly distinct entities,” which matches current antigen-based framing better than the older primary/secondary dichotomy [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[11.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/). The wording is appropriately cautious because the literature supports both a shared autoimmune principle and meaningful antigen-specific heterogeneity rather than a single universal downstream route [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[11.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[12.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/).

2. **(b) NELL1 omission and wrong frequency framing: PARTIALLY RESOLVED.**  
NELL1 is now included, and the sentence correcting the “under 1–4.9%” figure is directionally right: NELL1 frequencies are often far above that when the denominator is PLA2R-negative or PLA2R/THSD7A-negative disease [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factor–like-1-protein–positive-wang-sun/f6e85d3069095577b934153447ca82ad/) [[14.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/). But “a substantial further share” is imprecise across cohorts because published estimates range from **3.8%** of PLA2R/THSD7A-negative cases in one series to **35%** in Chinese cohorts, while whole-cohort primary-MN prevalence can be only **1.5–2%** in some populations [[4.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factor–like-1-protein–positive-wang-sun/f6e85d3069095577b934153447ca82ad/) [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/prevalence-of-neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-and-iwakura-ema/366a2a3e31465da3ad412bfb43fc911c/) [[11.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).

3. **(c) Anti-PLA2R titre, epitope spreading, non-IgG4 subclasses: RESOLVED.**  
The revised text now includes all three omitted elements, and each is supported. Anti-PLA2R levels correlate with disease activity and usually fall before proteinuria remission [[9.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[8.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[10.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/). Epitope spreading beyond CysR has been reported as an independent poor-prognosis marker, although newer work says its prognostic value beyond total antibody levels is not always superior [[10.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/) [[10.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/) [[10.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/). Non-IgG4 subclasses are common in PLA2R/THSD7A disease, and 2026 mechanistic work directly implicates **IgG1/IgG3** in complement-dependent cytotoxicity while IgG4 modulates rather than independently drives complement activation [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[15.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-value-of-pla2r-antigen-and-igg-subclass-staining-bajcsi-bitó/02d042ffec1e584f9d0cea8d35a37768/) [[16.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antipla2r-autoantibodies-induce-complement-activation-wu-tu/1f3dbe5db930500fa969bb3d70ff281d/).

4. **(d) Dated primary-versus-secondary framing: RESOLVED.**  
The revised summary now explicitly says the scope restriction is a curation choice and not a claim that the primary/secondary split is current best classification. That aligns with multiple reviews arguing that the traditional distinction has important limitations and is being replaced or supplemented by **antigen-based** nomenclature [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenic-spectrum-in-membranous-nephropathy-a-jain-tiwari/0f14bc45db215165b39c77afd0ad9815/) [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).

## Remaining Problems

- **“Podocyte surface antigen” is too broad.** PLA2R and THSD7A fit, but NELL1 is described as a **secreted, non-membrane-bound** protein and not routinely expressed by normal podocytes, so the sentence overgeneralizes across antigens [[11.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[11.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).
- **“In each case” is too strong.** The evidence base for antigen localization and serum/deposit IgG recognition is stronger for some antigens than others; the supplied corpus supports this clearly for PLA2R/THSD7A/NELL1, but not equally for every “rarer putative target” named in the sentence [[13.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[11.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/).
- **“Most inspected adult cases” for PLA2R is acceptable but soft.** Reported primary-MN prevalence is usually about **50–80%** or **65–70%**, so the wording is fair [[9.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[11.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).
- The final meta-sentence about “agent-inspected abstracts” and “uncalibrated appraisals” is **not a scientific claim** from the disease literature and does not belong in the summary itself.

## Omissions and Targeted Questions

A bounded summary of this scope should still mention that **NELL1 often shows IgG1-dominant or IgG1/IgG4-mixed deposits** and distinctive segmental/incomplete capillary-wall staining, because that is one of the clearest ways it differs from PLA2R-associated disease [[4.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[11.7]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[14.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/) [[14.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/). It should also avoid implying all “primary” antigens are podocyte-surface molecules, because newer antigen repertoires explicitly challenge that paradigm [[11.8]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/) [[11.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/how-times-have-changed-a-cornucopia-of-antigens-for-caza-al-rabadi/7584ae9158db505a8122b0d8f3de65bd/).

The complement characterization is **accurate with caveats** as of 2026. Human biopsy work shows signals from all three initiation pathways, with proximity ligation favoring the **classical pathway** in many PLA2R-associated cases [[12.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[12.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/). But experimental data also support an essential role for the **alternative pathway** in at least one mouse model, and review-level syntheses still treat pathway relevance as context- and model-dependent rather than universal [[17.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[17.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[18.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/complement-activation-and-effector-pathways-in-kistler-salant/6cba7f41d39e58e89e4536d1dc5705f4/). Likewise, C5b-9 remains plausible and important, but not conclusively established as the sole or universal dominant effector across human antigen-defined subtypes [[17.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[17.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[18.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/complement-activation-and-effector-pathways-in-kistler-salant/6cba7f41d39e58e89e4536d1dc5705f4/).

“**NELL-1 in a substantial further share of PLA2R-negative cases with primary-disease features**” is **directionally reasonable but too coarse**. It is accurate for some cohorts of PLA2R-negative or PLA2R/THSD7A-negative primary-like MN, where NELL1 accounts for roughly **16–35%** [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-protein-nell1-sethi-madden/c10783515d29517dbaca056a8c0ad5a0/) [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factor–like-1-protein–positive-wang-sun/f6e85d3069095577b934153447ca82ad/) [[14.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/). But it can **overstate** NELL1 if read as a universal frequency, because some cohorts report only **3.8–12.2%** of PLA2R/THSD7A-negative cases or **1.5–2%** of all primary MN [[4.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/) [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/prevalence-of-neural-epidermal-growth-factorlike-1-and-iwakura-ema/366a2a3e31465da3ad412bfb43fc911c/). It also **understates the malignancy caveat** if left unqualified: NELL1 is enriched for malignancy in several cohorts, including about **33%** in one large series and **26.1%** in another, although other Chinese cohorts found none, so the association is real but heterogeneous rather than obligatory [[4.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/nell1-is-a-target-antigen-in-malignancyassociated-caza-hassen/a9768ca7688a5549833dbd5aed09d7ce/) [[14.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-and-pathological-characteristics-of-li-liang/7f19bee613a15f468c4a45ca98347ab1/) [[6.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/neural-epidermal-growth-factor–like-1-protein–positive-wang-sun/f6e85d3069095577b934153447ca82ad/) [[7.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-clinicopathologic-study-of-neural-epidermal-growth-xu-hu/30399da5a89a572ab9d1c11442c2ca98/).

**NEW OVERALL VERDICT: consistent_with_caveats.**

The revised summary fixes the earlier omissions and substantially improves classification, NELL1, and serologic nuance, but it still needs tighter wording around **non-podocyte-surface antigens**, the breadth of support for “in each case,” and a more qualified one-clause description of **NELL1 frequency and malignancy association**.
